cases.sentence: Две дамы эти были ___ избранного нового петербургского кружка, называвшиеся, в подражание подражанию чему-то, les sept merveilles du monde.
cases.explain: «главные представительницы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The croquet party to which the Princess Tverskaya had invited Anna was to consist of two ladies and their adorers. These two ladies were the chief representatives of a select new Petersburg circle, nicknamed, in imitation of some imitation, les sept merveilles du monde. These ladies belonged to a circle which, though of the highest society, was utterly hostile to that in which Anna moved. Moreover, Stremov, one of the most influential people in Petersburg, and the elderly admirer of Liza Merkalova, was Alexey Alexandrovitch’s enemy in the political world. From all these considerations Anna had not meant to go, and the hints in Princess Tverskaya’s note referred to her refusal. But now Anna was eager to go, in the hope of seeing Vronsky.

cases.sentence: Кроме того, старый Стремов, один из ___ Петербурга, поклонник Лизы Меркаловой, был по службе враг Алексея Александровича.
cases.explain: «влиятельных людей» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.

cases.sentence: Не угодно ли пожаловать в сад? – доложил ___ в другой комнате.
cases.explain: «другой лакей» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “The princess is in the garden; they will inform her immediately. Would you be pleased to walk into the garden?” announced another footman in another room.

cases.sentence: Княгиня Тверская шла с Тушкевичем и родственницей барышней, к ___ провинциальных родителей проводившей лето у знаменитой княгини.
cases.explain: «великому счастию» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: The position of uncertainty, of indecision, was still the same as at home—worse, in fact, since it was impossible to take any step, impossible to see Vronsky, and she had to remain here among outsiders, in company so uncongenial to her present mood. But she was wearing a dress that she knew suited her. She was not alone; all around was that luxurious setting of idleness that she was used to, and she felt less wretched than at home. She was not forced to think what she was to do. Everything would be done of itself. On meeting Betsy coming towards her in a white gown that struck her by its elegance, Anna smiled at her just as she always did. Princess Tverskaya was walking with Tushkevitch and a young lady, a relation, who, to the great joy of her parents in the provinces, was spending the summer with the fashionable princess.

cases.sentence: Но в свете это самый ___, какого только я знаю, страстный игрок в крокет.
cases.explain: «любезный человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “No; you don’t care, perhaps, to meet Stremov? Let him and Alexey Alexandrovitch tilt at each other in the committee—that’s no affair of ours. But in the world, he’s the most amiable man I know, and a devoted croquet player. You shall see. And, in spite of his absurd position as Liza’s lovesick swain at his age, you ought to see how he carries off the absurd position. He’s very nice. Sappho Shtoltz you don’t know? Oh, that’s a new type, quite new.”

cases.sentence: И, несмотря на смешное его положение старого влюбленного в Лизу, надо видеть, как он выпутывается из этого ___!
cases.explain: «смешного положения» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.

cases.sentence: Бетси говорила все это, а между тем по веселому ___ ее Анна чувствовала, что она понимает отчасти ее положение и что-то затевает.
cases.explain: «умному взгляду» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Betsy said all this, and, at the same time, from her good-humored, shrewd glance, Anna felt that she partly guessed her plight, and was hatching something for her benefit. They were in the little boudoir.

cases.explain: «маленьком кабинете» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Betsy said all this, and, at the same time, from her good-humored, shrewd glance, Anna felt that she partly guessed her plight, and was hatching something for her benefit. They were in the little boudoir.

cases.sentence: Это вопрос ужасного ребенка, – и Бетти, видимо, хотела, но не могла удержаться и разразилась тем ___, каким смеются редко смеющиеся люди. – Надо у них спросить, – проговорила она сквозь слезы смеха.
cases.explain: «заразительным смехом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “You’re encroaching on Princess Myakaya’s special domain now. That’s the question of an enfant terrible,” and Betsy obviously tried to restrain herself, but could not, and went off into peals of that infectious laughter that people laugh who do not laugh often. “You’d better ask them,” she brought out, between tears of laughter.

cases.sentence: А что там дальше в ___, никто не хочет знать.
cases.explain: «самом деле» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “The husband? Liza Merkalova’s husband carries her shawl, and is always ready to be of use. But anything more than that in reality, no one cares to inquire. You know in decent society one doesn’t talk or think even of certain details of the toilet. That’s how it is with this.”

cases.sentence: Знаете, в ___ не говорят и не думают даже о некоторых подробностях туалета.
